name: Shehzad Roy
description:
'''Shehzad Roy''' (born 16 February 1977) is a [[Pakistani]] singer-songwriter, guitarist, activist, social worker, producer and humanitarian. He started his singing career in 1995 and has recorded six albums since. He has recorded many hit songs such as "Saali," "Teri Soorat" and "Kangna," but is most famous for his 2008 socio-political album ''[[Qismat Apnay Haath Mein]]''. Shehzad is also the president and founder of [[#Philanthropic work|Zindagi Trust]], a non-government charitable organisation, that strives to improve the quality of education available to the average Pakistani.

Shehzad has produced and hosted two documentary series, ''[[#Chal Parha|Chal Parha]]'', about the state of [[Education in Pakistan|public education in Pakistan]] and ''[[#Wasu aur Mein|Wasu aur Mein]]'', which follows the travels of Shehzad and a villager and deals with issues like progress, poverty and patriotism in Pakistan.

He received the [[Tamgha-i-Imtiaz]] (Medal of Excellence) in 2005, [[Civil decorations of Pakistan|Sitara-i-Eisaar]] (Star of Sacrifice) in 2006 and [[Sitara-i-Imtiaz]] (Star of Excellence) in 2018 from the [[Government of Pakistan]]. For his organisation's rehabilitation work after the [[2005 Kashmir earthquake]], he was awarded the Sitara-e-Eisaar in 2006. He was also selected to be a torch bearer for the 2008 [[Olympic Games]].
